data.title: Extending healthy life span--from yeast to humans
data.authors: Fontana L; Partridge L; Longo VD

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Influential review proposing that dietary restriction and reduced nutrient-sensing signalling (mTOR, GH/IGF-1) may slow ageing through similar, evolutionarily conserved mechanisms. Lifespan extension is shown in yeast, invertebrates, rodents and rhesus monkeys; in humans the evidence is limited to protective biomarker changes and genetic associations.
data.abstract_excerpt: When the food intake of organisms such as yeast and rodents is reduced (dietary restriction), they live longer than organisms fed a normal diet. A similar effect is seen when the activity of nutrient-sensing pathways is reduced by mutations or chemical inhibitors. In rodents, both dietary restriction and decreased nutrient-sensing pathway activity can lower the incidence of age-related loss of function and disease, including tumors and neurodegeneration.

extracted_findings.intervention: Not applicable (review – dietary restriction / nutrient-sensing inhibition)
extracted_findings.effect: Dietary restriction and reduced nutrient-sensing activity extend lifespan and reduce age-related disease
